She has been Team leader for planning and conducting training programs for Chief officers of Municipalities of Gujarat and active team member of PAS (Performance Assessment System for water and Sanitation), now C-WAS at CEPT

speakers.Name: N. Shanthi Maduresan
speakers.Bio: Mrs. N. Shanthi Maduresan is a distinguished leader in rural development and education, currently serving as the Chief Executive Officer of the DHAN Panchayat Development Programme. Based in Madurai, she has dedicated over three decades to strengthening grassroots institutions and empowering rural communities. She holds a Master’s degree in Rural Economics and Extension Education from Gandhigram Rural University, a B.Ed. from Annamalai University, and completed the Management Education Programme at IIM Ahmedabad in 2004. Her career began as a school teacher, followed by research work at Gandhigram Rural Institute, which grounded her in field-based development challenges. As a senior professional with DHAN Foundation, she has played a key role in designing and leading initiatives focused on local governance, community participation, and capacity building of Panchayats. Known for her integrative leadership, Mrs. Maduresan combines research, practice, and management to promote inclusive, sustainable, and self-reliant rural development.

speakers.Name: Nafisa Barot
speakers.Designation: Former Executive Director, Founder and Advisor
speakers.Bio: With four decades of experience in building and capacitating gender sensitive institutions for the empowerment of rural marginalized communities, Nafisa Barot is actively associated with the women’s and other people’s movements, influencing people and policies around water, gender justice and sustainable development. The desolate Bhal region of coastal Gujarat, where she along with three other women persevered to understand what options communities might have for development and hope, provided Nafisa with her real learning. Efforts in identifying and working with local women with a potential for leadership and with stamina to face the physical, social and environmental barriers to change, led them to co found Utthan in 1981. Today, Utthan has established its identity as an organization which has successfully demonstrated socio-technological alternatives that address the issues of the most marginalised. Nafisa has served on Government task forces of CAPART, NABARD, DWACRA, Planning Commission amongst a few. She is a founder Board member of several organisations and forums including Mahiti, Development Support Centre, Pravah and Working Group for Women & Land Ownership and India Wash Forum. She is currently on the Steering Committees of Water Conflict Forum and Mahila Kisan Adhikar Manch. She has published several articles on gender/water governance and community agency and been invited to speak at national and international forums.

speakers.Name: Namagembe Masitullah
speakers.Bio:
Masitullah Namagembe is a Grants and Research Assistant at the African Field Epidemiology Network (AFENET), where she blends her passion for community health with a strong commitment to evidence-based impact. Her journey into public health and development is shaped by lived experiences and a desire to support solutions that uplift vulnerable populations. She finds meaning in bringing together researchers, communities, and policymakers to co-create stronger, more resilient systems.
Alongside her role at AFENET, Masitullah consults with WaterConsults, providing subject matter expertise in business development on public health issues such as water security, sanitation, and climate resilience across Africa and the broader Global South. Working across sectors has deepened her belief in interdisciplinary collaboration as a key driver of meaningful change.
Driven by curiosity, empathy, and purpose, Masitullah hopes her work continues to foster shared learning, impactful partnerships, and community-centered solutions that strengthen both health and resilience.

speakers.Name: Navya Mistry
speakers.Bio:
I am a Youth Researcher at Jalchakra Innovations LLP, working at the intersection of water restoration, environmental sustainability, and nature-based solutions. I actively contribute to scientific research, field documentation, and policy-oriented studies focused on waterbody rejuvenation, soil health improvement, and ecosystem revival through innovative indigenous nature based technologies.
I have been involved in developing case studies, technical notes, and research-backed communication for Jalchakra’s government programs such as AMRUT 2.0, while also supporting international and national representations of Jalchakra Innovations at environmental forums and knowledge platforms. My work reflects a strong integration of science, sustainability, and societal impact.
My latest publication in Swadeshi Vigyan Patrika highlights indigenous, science-driven approaches to water and ecological restoration, reinforcing my commitment to evidence-based solutions rooted in Indian knowledge systems. I continue to work towards bridging research, on-ground implementation, and policy discourse for a sustainable future.

speakers.Name: Neeta Pokhrel
speakers.Organization: Water and Urban Development Sector, Asian Development Bank
speakers.Bio: Neeta Pokhrel is currently the Director of Water and Urban Development Sector Office at the Asian Development Bank (ADB). She leads the Pacific and Southeast Asia regional team at the Water and Urban Development Sector Office of ADB. An engineer by training; water, sanitation, climate change, and environmental optimist, and a passionate development worker, she has over 28 years of professional experience working with various organizations including the ADB, Bovis Lend Lease Pty Ltd Australia, engineering consulting firms, water utilities, and international non-government organizations.

speakers.Name: Neha Kumar
speakers.Organization: South Asia, Climate Bonds Initiative, India
speakers.Bio: Neha Kumar is the Head, South Asia, Climate Bonds Initiative and is based in Delhi. She steers policy, strategy and partnerships on climate risks and sustainable financial ecosystem in the region. Her efforts are targeted at building policy mechanisms, market infrastructure and capacities needed to accelerate financing for green, just and resilient transition. Her current areas of focus include transition and resilence finance, the role of financial policy and regulation, and DFIs and MDBs. Avidly interested in the political economy of flow of sustainable finance, she has been working on the topics of equity and climate justice. She has over twenty two years of experience in responsible financing, environmental and socio-political risks, serves on several policy and regulatory committees on climate finance and taxonomy. She is trained in science, international environmental negotiations and politics.

speakers.Name: Nitin Bassi
speakers.Organization: Council on Energy, Environment and Water, India
speakers.Bio:
Nitin is a Fellow for the Sustainable Water Team at The Council. He has more than 19 years of experience undertaking research, consultancy, and training in water resources. His work areas include river basin water accounting, agriculture water management, institutional and policy analysis in irrigation and water supply management, water quality analysis, climate-induced water risk assessment, and wetland management.

He was part of the delegation of the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India for the second Environment and Climate Sustainability Working Group Meeting under India’s G20 Presidency (2022-23). Additionally, he was a nominated member of the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India (GoI) Task Force that developed the White Paper on the U20 priority area 'Ensuring Water Security'.

He played a key role in establishing the India-EU Water Partnership and its work priority areas (2015-2020). He was a Member of the Water Quality Task Force (River Ganga), set up by the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, GoI (2017). He was also a Member of the thematic sub-group on Water Management for Climate-Smart Cities Assessment Framework 2.0, set up by the NIUA, MoHUA, GoI (2020-21). He is a core team member of the Delhi Water Forum which was launched in January 2023.

Before joining CEEW, he worked with the International Water Management Institute (IWMI) and the Institute for Resource Analysis and Policy. He has been engaged as a specialist in projects, research studies, and assignments supported by various national and international organisations including the European Commission, World Bank, GIZ, DFID, WRG 2030/IFC, UNICEF, WWF, IWMI, Fresh-Thoughts Consulting, DBT, SRTT, and SDTT.

He is a Natural Resource Management Specialist (M. Phil, M. Sc.) with more than 100 publications to his credit. He has co-edited five books, two of which were published by Routledge UK, two by Springer Nature, Switzerland, and one by Sage Publications. He regularly reviews manuscripts for Water Policy, International Journal of Water Resources Development, Journal of Hydrology, and book proposals for Routledge, Sage, Springer, and Wiley.

speakers.Name: Omkar Kane
speakers.Organization: Center for Water and Sanitation (CWAS), CRDF
speakers.Bio: Omkar has been associated with CWAS since 2016. He holds a Master’s degree in Infrastructure Engineering Design from CEPT University and has completed his graduation in Civil Engineering from Pune University. He has multidisciplinary consulting experience in the field of urban and infrastructure planning, project implementation, and public policy. At CWAS he has worked directly with Sinnar Municipal Council in making the city ODF and moving towards ODF++. Currently, he is involved in the overall coordination, monitoring, and management of ODF++ activities for ULBs under Pune Division in Maharashtra and also supports the state unit in a technical capacity. He has previous experience in design of water supply and sewerage projects,  the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna, and transport system planning.

speakers.Name: Osward Chanda
speakers.Bio: Osward brings over 30 years of expertise in water and sanitation, with two decades spent in senior management positions encompassing development finance, utility regulation, and institutional change management. He served as Director of the Water at the African Development Bank, he expanded the department’s portfolio to $5.5 billion, annual lending to $1 billion, and led a special fund for project preparation. He oversaw the development and implementation of policies and strategies to improve inclusive access, foster public-private partnerships, and strengthen climate change resilience. In Zambia, Osward was instrumental in pioneering sector reforms, utility regulation and building strategic partnerships, successfully raising more than $170 million for a pro-poor Trust Fund. A committed mentor, he holds degrees from the University of Melbourne and the University of Zambia.

speakers.Name: Pablo Morales-Rico
speakers.Organization: Center for Research and Advanced Studies of the National Polytechnic Institute (Cinvestav), Mexico
speakers.Bio:
Pablo Morales-Rico, Ph.D. (Cinvestav, Mexico), has extensive experience in environmental projects expert with a strong focus in wastewater treatment and greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation. His doctoral research focused on developing innovative methods to quantify and mitigate GHG emissions in large-scale wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs).
Dr. Morales-Rico's professional experience spans both public and private sectors. He has led diverse water management initiatives, including the supervision of the largest WWTP in Latin America, and has directed projects for key institutions like the National Water Commission (CONAGUA) and the Secretariat of Infrastructure, Communications and Transport (SICT).
He is a published author of several peer-reviewed articles and actively presents his research internationally. Dr. Morales-Rico is a consultant for the National Association of Water and Sanitation Companies (ANEAS) in Mexico and is an active member of the International Water Association and the Climate Resilient Sanitation Coalition, contributing to global efforts in water and climate resilience

speakers.Name: Patrick Moriarty
speakers.Bio: Patrick Moriarty is Chief Executive Officer of IRC, an international think-and-do tank dedicated to building strong national water, sanitation and hygiene systems. He also serves as Chair of the Steering Committee of Sanitation and Water for All (SWA), a global partnership uniting governments, civil society, the private sector and development partners to realise the human rights to water and sanitation. Patrick has over three decades of experience working with governments and utilities, with a particular focus on service delivery, finance and governance for climate-resilient, inclusive WASH services at scale. A recognised systems leader and coalition-builder, he works to connect local innovation with national and global reform, and is committed to putting evidence, politics and people at the centre of decision-making. He is a regular advisor and speaker at global water forums.

speakers.Name: Pranjali Chowdhary
speakers.Organization: Institute for Governance and Sustainable Development
speakers.Bio: I hold a Master’s degree in Public Policy from St. Xavier’s and currently work as a Policy and Research Professional at the Institute for Governance & Sustainable Development (IGSD). My work focuses on climate change and air quality, with a particular emphasis on short-lived climate pollutants such as methane and black carbon. I primarily work on waste management and sub-national, sectoral mitigation strategies in India, supporting research, policy analysis, and capacity building to advance near-term climate action and sustainable development.

speakers.Name: Priyadarshini Choudhary
speakers.Organization: Center for Water and Sanitation (CWAS), CRDF
speakers.Bio: Priyadarshini has been associated with CWAS since 2022. She has over ten years of experience in managing multidisciplinary infrastructure projects. Her core competencies are in project management, coordination and documentation. At CWAS, she is primarily involved in research work related to emerging fields in WASH such as ESG and water security assessments. She has a Master’s Degree in Infrastructure Engineering & Management from CEPT University, Ahmedabad, and Bachelors in Civil Engineering from Rajasthan University, Jaipur.

speakers.Name: Priyambda Tripathy
speakers.Bio: Priyambda is a Ph.D. and Masters in Social Work from Tiss, Mumbai. She has more than 15 years of experience in Government Advisory, Social Research, and Project Management. She has worked with diverse organizations and her research interests include Collective Action Models such as grass root organizations (FPO, Self Help Groups), Social Exclusion, and Public Policy

speakers.Name: Priyansh Singh
speakers.Bio: Priyansh Singh is a second-year student pursuing Bachelor's in Civil Engineering at CEPT University, Ahmedabad. He has a keen interest in researching and implementing smart automation methods and strategies to increase operational efficiency and real-time monitoring capabilities in systems. He has worked on projects addressing real world challenges by introducing scalable solutions that offer effective alternatives to manual operations, while reducing maintenance requirements and operational hazards. One of his notable works includes an algorithm which is capable of detecting leakage regions in a pipe network using only outlet flow sensors, along with an alert system, which is scalable at a smaller as well as larger scale, providing a smart solution to detect pipe leakage in the water network. His aim is to propose innovative methods that replace the old methods by implementing automation in civil engineering.

speakers.Name: Rajas Kolhatkar
speakers.Bio: Rajas Kolhatkar is a public policy professional working at the intersection of water quality, community engagement, and public systems. He is a Fellow with the International Innovation Corps (IIC), placed with the Development Innovation Lab (DIL-India) at the University of Chicago, where he supports implementation-focused work on in-line chlorination and rural water safety. He brings a governance lens to program design and delivery, working with government counterparts and community institutions to translate field realities into practical, scalable approaches. His interests include equity in service delivery, frontline systems, and institutional reform.

speakers.Name: Rajib Das
speakers.Bio:
Dr. Rajib Das is currently working as the MEL Lead at the Centre for Advocacy and
Research (CFAR), where he oversees data, documentation, and knowledge
generation across multiple projects, focusing on WASH-climate linkages,
occupational health, non-communicable diseases, gender-based violence, and social
inclusion, across Indian states. His work spans interdisciplinary fields, and his
impactful publications, featured in esteemed journals, explore diverse topics,
including cultural compulsion in sanitation, spatial inequality in the standard of living
in urban areas, and women's empowerment in India. Previously, he worked as a
Senior Research Fellow at TRCSS, JNU, and also as an Associate at I-PAC,
Kolkata. By training, he is a Geographer and Demographer; he holds a MPhil and a
PhD degree from Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi.

speakers.Name: Rajul Gajjar
speakers.Bio:
Dr. Rajul K. Gajjar is an eminent academic leader and a distinguished figure in the field of engineering education, with over four decades of experience in academia, research, and administration. She has significantly contributed to the advancement of engineering and technical education in India. Dr. Gajjar has an extensive research background with over 66 National and International Research Publications, four authored books, and three granted patents to her credit. She has supervised more than 30 PG and 8 Doctoral students and led over 38 high-impact projects, covering areas such as international collaborations, Centers of Excellence, research innovation, accreditation, and ranking frameworks for excellence in engineering education.
Her contributions to research and innovation are evident in GTU’s outstanding achievements, including publishing 160+ patents, 1,700 registered Ph.D. scholars, and 683 research articles in SCI journals. Before assuming the role of Vice Chancellor at GTU, Dr. Gajjar served as the Principal of L.D. College of Engineering and other Government Engineering Colleges in Gujarat. She also held key administrative positions such as Additional Commissioner of the Education Department, Government of Gujarat, and Officiating Vice Chancellor of the Teacher’s University.

speakers.Name: Ramnath Jha
speakers.Bio:
Dr. Ramanath Jha is Distinguished Fellow at Observer Research Foundation, Mumbai. He works on urbanisation — urban sustainability, urban governance and urban planning.

Dr. Jha belongs to the 1977 batch of the Indian Administrative Service. During his time at the IAS —through the 1980s and 1990s — he was Administrator, Pandharpur Municipal Council; Administrator and Municipal Commissioner, Solapur; Collector and Deputy Director Municipal Administration, Ahmednagar; Municipal Commissioner, Pune; and Metropolitan Commissioner, MMRDA. His subsequent postings were as Regional Advisor, South Asia for the Urban Management Programme of the UNDP/UN-Habitat; Vice Chairman and Managing Director at MSRDC; and Principal Secretary, Transport, Ports and State Excise, Government of Maharashtra.

He received the state government’s Chinmulgund Award for Administrative Excellence in 1989. He sought voluntary retirement from government in 2008 and joined the private sector as CEO & MD, Khed Economic Infrastructure Pvt Ltd.

Dr. Jha has co-authored the books — Towards People Friendly Cities — published by UNICEF; Urban Essays, published by YASHADA and co-edited Perspectives in Urban Development, published by Capital Publishing Company. He has published a number of papers on a variety of urban subjects and has widely lectured on urban issues.

speakers.Name: Ravie Kiran Bokam
speakers.Bio: Ravie is a gender rights advocate, currently leading the Urban WASH project in Rajasthan, India. With more than 15 years of experience in the social development sector, he focuses on inclusive GEDSI-WASH, health, and social inclusion. Ravie provides technical guidance, manages partnerships, and implements strategies for community engagement. As part of this effort, he and the team developed a community-centred WASH governance model supported by community monitoring to ensure climate resilient inclusive WASH. Under his leadership, a comprehensive menstrual hygiene management initiative focussing on gender inclusive and climate informed model was implemented in Jaipur.

speakers.Name: Ria Triany
speakers.Organization: Environmental Agency of Jakarta City Government
speakers.Bio:
Environmental professional with over 15 years of experience in urban environmental governance, water and sanitation systems, and sustainable development.
Currently serving at the Jakarta Environmental Agency. Since 2025, I lead initiatives that promote environmental compliance and community engagement, including the ECO Act (Education, Collaboration, Action) and Green Culinary Cawang programs.
I hold a Master of Science in Urban Water & Sanitary Engineering from IHE Delft, The Netherlands. My professional interest lies in bridging public policy and practical implementation — supporting inclusive, measurable, and impactful sustainability programs across government, academia/reserach, Social Change Organization (SCO), and business sectors.

speakers.Name: Rishi Bakshi
speakers.Organization: Institute for Governance and Sustainable Development
speakers.Bio:
With an academic background in development and sustainability from Azim Premji University, Rishi Ranjan Bakshi is working as a Consultant on the waste sector at the Institute for Governance & Sustainable Development (IGSD). His work focuses on solid waste management, circular economy approaches, and near-term climate mitigation in India.
 
In his current role, he supports research and policy-oriented analysis related to waste sector interventions, with a focus on advancing evidence-based approaches for waste reduction and landfill diversion. Previously, he worked on circular economy initiatives with Saahas NGO, contributing to community-level waste management and resource recovery efforts. He has also worked with Selco Foundation, supporting rural communities on the integration of decentralized solar energy technologies in the agriculture sector.

speakers.Name: Rushabh Shah
speakers.Bio:
I am Rushabh Shah, a final-year Bachelor of Architecture student at the Faculty of Architecture, SCET, Surat. My academic work focuses on the intersection of built environment, climate, health, and everyday labour within craft-based settlements. I have represented my institution at national platforms such as the NASA Design Competitions, Louis I Kahn Trophy, HUDCO Design Trophy, and NIUA Poster Competition, with multiple national-level recognitions.
My ongoing undergraduate thesis examines the silk-weaving town of Sualkuchi, Assam, analyzing housing typologies, ventilation, water and sanitation practices, and occupational health conditions of local and migrant weavers. Through detailed field documentation, spatial mapping, and interviews, the research investigates how climate stress and informal WASH infrastructure influence well-being in dense living-working environments.
I am interested in research-led architectural approaches that address climate resilience, health equity, and socially responsive settlement design in the Global South.

speakers.Name: S.M. Vijayanand
speakers.Bio: Mr. Vijayanand is an officer of the 1981 batch of the IAS, belonging to the Kerala cadre. Almost his entire career was in Rural Development, Local Governance, and Decentralized Planning. He coordinated Kerala's People's Planning for fifteen years. During this period he nurtured Kudumbashree, a highly successful SHG programme in the country and was active in moulding the Kerala Institute of Local Administration (KILA) into an institution of excellence in the training of Elected Representatives. As Secretary of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj during 2015-16, he was instrumental in introducing the Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP) in the country.

speakers.Name: Sagar gupta
speakers.Bio: Sagar Gupta is a Guest Faculty at the University College of Engineering, Govind Guru Tribal University (GGTU), with expertise in sanitation and sustainable infrastructure. He brings over 10 years of experience across academia, consultancy, and research. Sagar has contributed to curriculum development, student mentoring, and applied research, effectively bridging theory with real-world practice. He is a co-inventor of a German patent for a smart methane potential measurement device and has hands-on experience in innovative waste-to-resource technologies, including sludge-to-biochar conversion. He is a member of the International Water Association (IWA), Institution of Engineers (India) (IEI), and the Sustainable Sanitation Alliance (SuSanA).

speakers.Name: Sagar Patil
speakers.Organization: All India Institute of Local Self Government, Mumbai
speakers.Bio:
Mr. Sagar Patil holds a Master’s in Technology in Civil - Environmental Engineering and works as the Senior Technical Officer at AIILSG, Mumbai. With over 11 years of experience in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), his expertise spans faecal sludge management (FSM), used water (wastewater) management and solid waste management.
He has worked extensively with government, private, NGO, and CSR stakeholders on advocacy, planning, technical design, management, and implementation of waste management projects. As a skilled capacity builder, he has organized and conducted training programs for government and private officials/engineers on used water management, FSM, and occupational health and safety. Additionally, he has been involved in research projects focused on faecal sludge treatment and wastewater management. He deeply understands government policies, guidelines, and missions in the WASH sector.

speakers.Name: Saidou Djibo Mahamane Moustapha
speakers.Organization: NGO Facilitation of National and Cross-Border Transhumance for Pastoralists (FAT-TRANS-BIGGAL)
speakers.Bio: Saidou Djibo Mahamane Moustapha is a committed leader and the President of the NGO FAT-TRANS-BIGGAL, where he works to protect pastoralists, support secure transhumance, and strengthen rural communities living in insecure areas. With more than 12 years of experience in communication, project coordination, and community mobilization, he has also served as Communication Advisor with JSI. Trained as a socio-anthropologist, he conducts research on access to drinking water and sanitation in rural areas. Passionate about local development, peacebuilding, and resilience, he uses his expertise to improve the living conditions of vulnerable populations across Niger.

speakers.Name: Sakshi Gudwani
speakers.Bio: Sakshi Gudwani works with the Gates Foundation as a Senior Program Officer and manages the Foundation’s Water, Sanitation & Hygiene (WSH) program in India. She has a diverse set of experiences that spans across private, public, and nonprofit sector work. She has been a development professional for over 10 years and focuses on policy & program design, institutional strengthening, and private sector engagement. At the Gates Foundation, Sakshi also worked with the Avahan program - Foundation’s flagship HIV prevention program in India. Before joining the Foundation, she worked with The Boston Consulting Group (BCG). At BCG, she was a part of multiple teams which counselled CEOs, government ministries and top management across industries on critical business problems. During this time, she worked across Social, Healthcare, Technology and Financial Services sectors. Sakshi has an engineering degree and is a management graduate of the Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Lucknow.

speakers.Name: Saloni Srivastava
speakers.Bio: With an academic background in economics and sustainable development from the Geneva Graduate Institute, Saloni Srivastava is serving as a Senior Research and Policy Associate at the Institute for Governance & Sustainable Development (IGSD). Her work focuses on advancing evidence-based policymaking to support near-term climate mitigation strategies in India. In her role, she supports research, policy analysis, and stakeholder engagement on methane mitigation from the waste sector, policies to reduce the climate and public health impacts of waste, and climate finance policies and instruments that enable effective climate action.

speakers.Name: Sangita Bose Das
speakers.Organization: Hooghly Chinchurah Municipality, (UD & MA Dept. West Bengal)
speakers.Bio:
Sangita Bose Das is an Urban Planner at Hooghly-Chinsurah Municipality, West Bengal with over 17 years of professional experience in urban infrastructure and municipal services. She holds a Master’s degree in Geography from Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University. She has done course on Urban Management from IIT Kharagpur and Urban Planning and Management from the University of Calcutta.
Her professional work involves planning and implementation of urban development projects, particularly in housing, land-use planning, basic urban services, and solid waste management. She focuses on addressing field-level challenges and ensuring effective implementation of government policies at the municipal level. She has actively engaged in project monitoring, coordination and policy implementation at the municipal level. 
She has undergone multiple professional training programmes at the Administrative Training Institute (ATI), Government of West Bengal. Her areas of interest include sustainable urban development, participatory planning, and inclusive urban governance.

speakers.Name: Santanu Das
speakers.Bio: Santanu Das, is working as a Scientist/Engineer-SE at NE-SAC has 13 years of Experience across government administration and the private sector. He specializes in leveraging space technology to drive sustainable urban development. His expertise lies in applying geospatial intelligence to urban and regional planning, enabling data-driven decision-making for large-scale operations in planning, scheduling, and implementation. With a strong engineering foundation and a Master’s degree in City Planning from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, He brings an in-depth understanding of how satellite data and spatial analytics can transform urban systems, support infrastructure development, and enhance governance efficiency.

speakers.Name: Satish Jung Shahi
speakers.Designation: CWIS Alliance Nepal (CWISAN) Secretariat Coordination Officer

speakers.Name: Saubiya Sareshwala
speakers.Organization: Center for Water and Sanitation (CWAS), CRDF
speakers.Bio: Saubiya has been associated with CWAS since 2019. She has experience in various aspects of municipal finance like budgets, investment planning, property tax, and gender budgeting. She is currently exploring the idea of shadow credit rating for urban local bodies and climate finance. She also works in the water sector, offering city-level support in preparing water-secure and water balance plans. She holds a Master’s degree in Urban Planning with infrastructure specialization from CEPT University and a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering from LJ Institute of Engineering & Technology with one year of experience in teaching and academics. Her areas of interest include financing urban development, climate finance, and participatory WASH governance.

speakers.Name: Saurabh Bhatt
speakers.Bio:
Saurabh’s principal field is Environmental Planning, with a focus on exploring the interactions between urban areas, the environment, urban sociology, and public participation. He holds a master’s degree in Planning (specialisation in Environmental Planning) from the School of Planning and Architecture, New Delhi. Saurabh has led research-oriented academic and professional experiences.
As a Research Associate at the Centre for Urban Studies, Indian Institute of Public Administration, Saurabh contributed to impactful projects, including a Women’s Safety Audit in Ghaziabad, advancing blue-green infrastructure initiatives, and devising innovative waste management strategies for Varanasi. Guided by a calm sense of continuity and purpose, he is committed to shaping inclusive and sustainable urban futures.

speakers.Name: Shalini Sinha
speakers.Bio:
Dr. Shalini Sinha is the Principal Researcher and Center Head of the Center of Excellence in Urban Transport (CoE-UT).  She is the Program Chair- Master of Urban Transport Systems and an Associate Professor at the Faculty of Planning, CEPT University. She is a Transport and Urban Planner with around twenty years of experience in India and the UK.

Dr. Shalini brings her extensive experience to bear on improving research, advisory, and capacity building related to the aspects of transport and urban planning for the built environment.  She has worked on a number of urban transport and urban planning projects.  More recently, Dr. Shalini has been involved in the BRT projects for Hubli Dharwad, Surat, Vadodara, and  Ahmedabad.

She has also been involved in demand modelling for Metro projects in Surat and Ahmedabad as well as in research projects related to strategic transport planning, integrated land use transport strategies, demand modelling and public transport network planning. Her research interests lie in transport policy and practice, transport modelling, economic appraisals and public transport planning.

Dr. Shalini has also been associated with several capacity building programs in urban transport. She is a Member of the IHT (The Institution of Highways and Transportation), U.K and an Associate Member of the Institute of Town Planners, India.

Dr. Shalini has also undergone a Professional Certificate Course in Public Transport Management in Singapore and has successfully completed a Trainer Programme in Case Teaching by The World Bank in Washington.  She has a PhD from CEPT University and a Master's degree in Transport Planning and Engineering from the University of Leeds, U.K.

speakers.Name: Sheetal Walvekar
speakers.Bio: I am an academician, researcher, and policy expert, I possess advanced expertise in overseeing research initiatives, spearheading academic-policy partnerships, and conducting interdisciplinary analyses on science & technology, sustainability, governance, and development. I have shown proficiency in securing competitive funding, cultivating cross-sector alliances, and guiding emerging talent in the field of public policy. Proficiency in mixed-methods research, stakeholder analysis, impact evaluation, and policy communication.

speakers.Name: Shishir Gupta
speakers.Organization: Centre for Social and Economic Progress
speakers.Bio: Shishir Gupta is a Senior Fellow at the Centre for Social and Economic Progress, New Delhi. As a Senior Fellow, Shishir has led research on multiple themes – the role of large firms in India’s economic growth, states’ growth in India, housing affordability, media reporting, and the role of funding in determining the cleanliness of Indian cities. Currently, he is developing a new research vertical on the competitiveness of India’s corporates and cities. India’s per capita GDP must grow at 7.5 percent p.a. to achieve the Viksit Bharat aspiration by 2047. Since corporates are responsible for production and are mostly located in urban areas, realising the goal implies making our corporates and cities globally competitive. Prior to CSEP, Shishir was with McKinsey Global Institute for 14 years. He is an economist by training, with MA, and MPhil from Delhi School of Economics.

speakers.Name: Shruthi Gurumoorthy
speakers.Bio: Shruthi Gurumoorthy is a development professional and has completed her graduation and post-graduation in Social Work from the University of Delhi and Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai. She has worked with NGOs, and policy think tanks and has been part of a reputed Delhi Government Fellowship. Her interests include caste and gender.

speakers.Name: Silver Mugisha
speakers.Organization: National Water and Sewerage Corporation, Uganda
speakers.Bio:
Dr. Eng. Silver Mugisha is the Managing Director of National Water and Sewerage Corporation (NWSC) Uganda, one for the well performing water and sanitation utilities in Africa.
Mugisha holds a Ph.D. in Engineering and Economics of Makerere University - Uganda; MSc in Sanitary Engineering (Sector Utility Management) from IHE Delft-Netherlands; and BSc. Civil Engineering - Makerere University - Uganda. His PhD research, which was carried out in collaboration with PURC of University of Florida, USA focused on areas of performance monitoring, incentive design and productivity analysis. 
Dr. Mugisha brings over 30 years of industry leadership, organizational transformation expertise and excutive management experience to one of the well performing utilities in Africa.
Dr. Mugisha has worked and supported, organizational and performance improvement, for various organizations in Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Rwanda, India, and Trinidad and Tobago among others. 
Dr Mugisha is very active in the water sector as well as in the community. He was a Board Member of the International Water Association (IWA), 2014-2016 and later become the Vice President of IWA (2016-2018).
 He is the President Emeritus of the African Water and Sanitation Association (AfWASA) (2020-2025). He is also the Chairman Emeritus of the following Boards; Governing Council of the Federation of Uganda Employers (FUE); Uganda Business and Technical Examinations Board (UBTEB), Uganda Technical College Bushenyi, and a Board member of Umeme Ltd (an electricity distributor).

He is currently a Board member of National Security Fund (NSSF), a registered engineer with Engineers Registration Board (ERB), and a member of Uganda Institute of Professional Engineers (UIPE). 
Dr Mugisha is a Fellow of the International Water Association and Sense Research School of the Netherlands. He is the author of more than 50 peer reviewed papers, two books, and chapters of books published internationally.
He is very passionate about service delivery, knowledge and professional development. His leadership and commitment have been key in helping many water utilities especially in Africa on their drive towards water and sanitation for All.

speakers.Name: Sradha Das
speakers.Bio:
Sradha Das is a development professional with over 12 years of experience in the social sector, working across public health, nutrition, and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) programs. She holds a Post Graduate in Rural Management from KIIT University, Odisha, and has been actively involved in designing, implementing and monitoring community-centric interventions with a focus on resilience, sustainability, and equity.
Currently based in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, she works closely with government systems and communities to strengthen climate-resilient WASH infrastructures. Her work reflects a strong grounding in field realities and lived experiences of vulnerable communities.
Outside of work, she values creativity and balance in everyday life and enjoys spending time at home where painting and cooking are shared interests within her family.

speakers.Name: Srijana Karki
speakers.Bio: Srijana Karki is a senior development professional and female entrepreneur with over a decade of experience advancing gender equality, disability, and social inclusion (GEDSI) across the WASH, human rights, and humanitarian sectors in Nepal and South Asia. Bridging development practice with private-sector leadership, she champions the integration of GEDSI into business, Women Empowerment Principle, investment, and policy frameworks, grounded in her belief that economic empowerment is essential to achieving gender equality. She currently serves as a Technical Gender Advisor, Board of Director, across multiple enterprises led by women, promoting inclusive and gender-responsive business models. Srijana holds master’s degrees in Gender Studies and Rural Development and is a recipient of the Samajsewa Ratna Shree National Award (2022) and the Australian Government Award for Climate Change and Water (2023)

speakers.Name: Sujoy Chaudhury
speakers.Bio: A civil engineer by training and an aspiring social scientist, Sujoy has nearly three decades of experience in the development sector spanning national and international geographies, corporate, bi-lateral, international and national organizations in the Shelter, DM, WASH, Livelihoods, DRR and CCA domains. Sujoy is currently the co-founder of the Centre for Sustainable Solutions [ CSS] a non-profit working on an action – research mode with focus on rural communities in low-elevation coastal zones to strengthen the science- policy- society interface. CSS works in alignment with the 20230 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction.

speakers.Name: Suren Vakil
speakers.Bio:
Suren Vakil is an accomplished professional in infrastructure engineering consultancy with over 35 years of experience in the UK and India. He has a distinguished career managing infrastructure projects, including significant contributions to disaster management after the Gujarat earthquake and developing containers and LNG terminals. His portfolio includes more than 400 projects in over twenty-five countries and technical specialisation in water pollution control and wastewater engineering. Suren has established and led Indian operations for prominent UK-based international companies, Babtie Group and BMT (British Maritime Technology). Throughout his career, he has successfully guided teams in ports, logistics, and environmental sectors. He has vast hands-on experience with PPP infrastructure projects in the UK and India.

He currently serves as the Vice-Chairperson of the CEPT Research & Development Foundation. As Vice-Chairperson, Suren is responsible for providing strategic leadership and enhancing governance capabilities and operational systems to ensure CRDF delivers high-quality outcomes. He is also committed to promoting and strengthening a culture of research and collaboration within CRDF.

His academic background includes a Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering and a Master's in Environmental Engineering from Leeds University. He is a UK-certified chartered engineer and chartered environmental manager and has previously represented the Institution of Civil Engineers in a regional capacity. He also has a Certificate in Company Directorship from the UK Institute of Directors. 

Suren has a keen interest in reading history and popular science, and he enjoys capturing moments through amateur photography.

speakers.Name: Tanay Chopra
speakers.Bio: Tanay Chopra is an urban designer from CEPT University, Ahmedabad, and is currently working as a Junior Urban Designer at Metabolic Office, Ahmedabad. His academic work has focused on climate change challenges, particularly heat and flooding. His co-authored research paper, “Assessment of Co-Benefits of Water Bodies in India,” integrates ecological, social, and spatial parameters supported by GIS-based analysis and examines water bodies across different ownership and governance frameworks. He has previously interned at BDP India and has also co-authored a research paper accepted by AESOP and the University of Toronto. His broader interests lie at the intersection of urban policy and climate adaptation

speakers.Name: Tania Thankam Mathew
speakers.Bio: I am a Master of Planning Student with a background in engineering, specializing in housing. My dissertation work focuses on resilient WASH solutions by examining sanitation challenges in coastal and flood-prone regions, with specific reference to zoning patterns along the Kerala Coast. Then assesses decentralized and climate responsive sanitation systems based on risk-sensitive zoning and land-use characteristics. The work forms the basis for continued thesis research towards developing a zoning based resilient sanitation framework for vulnerable coastal areas.

speakers.Name: Tsitsi Prudence Humanikwa
speakers.Bio: Tsitsi Prudence Humanikwa is a dedicated Geographical Information Science (GIS) Specialist and Lecturer at Lupane State University, Zimbabwe. She holds a MSc in Population Informatics and Analytics and a BSc in Geographical Information Science and Earth Observations from the University of Zimbabwe. Her research passion focuses on leveraging geo-technologies to address critical demographic, food security and climate change issues for intervention initiatives and policy-making, thereby contributing to sustainable development. As she continues her academic journey, Ms. Humanikwa is eager to contribute to the advancement of GIS research and development through research, teaching and community engagement.

speakers.Name: Tushar Chakrabarty
speakers.Bio: Tushar has a five-year experience working in the field of public finance. He has worked extensively with finances of the central and state governments and has authored multiple publications. At Janaagraha, his work relates to municipal finance and leveraging resources for better mobilisation of municipal own source revenues.

speakers.Name: Umra Anees
speakers.Bio: Ms. Umra Anees is an Urban Planner who graduated from the School of Planning and Architecture, Delhi, in 2018. She is currently associated with Centre for Science and Environment, where she works on research, advocacy, and capacity-building initiatives across various themes related to urban water and wastewater management. She brings nearly nine years of professional experience, with strong exposure to solid waste management, WASH, and slum upgradation. Previously, she has worked with the Centre for Urban and Regional Excellence (CURE) and the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), contributing to projects such as Improving Access to Taps and Toilets in Noida slums, Swachh Bharat Mission exposure workshops, and the Sanitation Capacity Building Platform.

speakers.Name: Upasana Yadav
speakers.Organization: Center for Water and Sanitation (CWAS), CRDF
speakers.Bio: Upasana has been associated with CWAS since 2014. She has extensive experience in WASH and urban development sector. She leads CWAS’s work in implementation of city sanitation plans, WASH improvement planning tools, and innovative financing mechanisms like development impact bonds and blended finance mechanism. She also has experience in water security, performance assessment systems, public finance and business models. She has worked with governments and sector partners for planning and implementation of WASH programmes. She has a Masters in Planning (Infrastructure) from CEPT University, Ahmedabad, and a Bachelors in Civil Engineering from MS University, Vadodara. Prior to joining CWAS, she has worked as an urban planner at SAI consulting Engineers Ltd. and as a construction engineer in Essar project (I) Ltd.

speakers.Name: Utkarsha Kavadi
speakers.Organization: All India Institute of Local Self Government

speakers.Name: Uzra Sultana
speakers.Bio: Uzra holds a Master’s degree in Environmental Sciences and brings nearly 18 years of professional experience across environmental research, climate change initiatives, WASH, content development and project management. She began her career in 2004 at the Environmental Management and Policy Research Institute (EMPRI), Bangalore, and contributed to applied research and policy-oriented environmental work. In 2011, she joined the Administrative Staff College of India (ASCI), Hyderabad, where she played a key role in developing City Sanitation Plans for eight cities in Karnataka, supporting urban sanitation planning and governance processes. Since 2013, Uzra has been part of Arghyam, working towards safe and sustainable water and sanitation solutions across Indian towns and cities. Currently, she leads initiatives on Jal Jeevan Mission’s source sustainability and rural greywater management, focusing on applying digital tools, scientific planning and scalable approaches to strengthen long-term water security outcomes in rural India.

speakers.Name: Vanshika Bajaj
speakers.Bio: Vanshika Bajaj is an Architect with a specialisation in Urban Regeneration. Her expertise spans across research, spatial mapping, and policy analysis. In her current role as a Research Assistant with the Sanitation Capacity Building Platform (SCBP) at the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), she contributes to advancing inclusive sanitation initiatives through research, development of knowledge products, and capacity building at national and regional levels. Her work involves supporting the design of research methodologies, undertaking field data collection and analysis, and developing GIS-based analytical outputs to inform planning for inclusive and sustainable water and sanitation systems. Academically, Vanshika was awarded the Merit Excellence Scholarship for securing first position throughout her master’s programme at the Faculty of Architecture, Jamia Millia Islamia, where her thesis focused on the ecological regeneration of the Naini Lake Basin, Uttarakhand. She has prior professional experience working on Local Area Master Plans for informal settlements in Delhi and SAAR Sameeksha Project under the SAAR Initiative of Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, contributing to impact assessment studies undertaken as part of the Smart Cities Mission. She has also supported spatial mapping of settlements, heritage assets, and water bodies for the formulation of Heritage Bye-laws for Mehrauli under the National Monuments Authority. Her work reflects a strong interest in bridging research, spatial evidence, and policy to support sustainable and equitable urban development.

speakers.Name: Vasu Saha
speakers.Bio: A public policy professional, Vasu Saha specialises in municipal finance with a strong focus on enhancing own-source revenues for urban local governments. At Janaagraha, he co-led the advisory engagement with the 5th Karnataka State Finance Commission (SFC) and 6th Odisha SFC for recommending own source revenue augmentation reforms. He has previously worked on property tax and user charge reforms in Assam, Jharkhand, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

speakers.Name: Vinay Kumar
speakers.Bio: Vinay Kumar is a Senior Manager at Waste Warriors Society, a nonprofit organization working to solve the waste crisis in the Indian Himalayan region, including Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. He has been associated with Waste Warriors for over six and a half years, playing a key role in strengthening on-ground operations. Vinay works closely on designing and implementing sustainable solid waste management systems, focusing on both centralized and decentralized models. His expertise includes developing solutions that balance CAPEX and OPEX sustainability, ensuring long-term operational viability. Through his work, Vinay contributes to building efficient, scalable, and environmentally responsible waste management systems suited to fragile mountain ecosystems.

speakers.Name: Xerxes Rao
speakers.Bio:
Xerxes Rao is the Vice President of Urban Planning at Urban Management Centre, has 16 years of diverse experience in urban development, governance, and infrastructure projects. His extensive career includes collaboration with multilateral institutions, central and state governments, para-statal agencies, and urban local bodies. 

Xerxes provides technical support to the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, with a particular emphasis on converging the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM) and Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), including initiatives related to Self-Help Groups (SHGs). His expertise extends to the integration of women led community-driven efforts, reflected in projects emphasizing community participation, urban governance, and infrastructure development. 

Xerxes, a guest faculty at LBSNAA and lecturer at institutions like Xavier’s University Bhubaneshwar, has degrees in architecture and project management from Vallabh Vidyanagar and the University of Stuttgart, Germany. He holds a diploma in project management from IIMA.

speakers.Name: Yashna Arora
speakers.Bio: Yashna (he/they) is a trans researcher and writer from Delhi-Lucknow. He has been an Urban Fellow at the Indian Institute for Human Settlements, Bengaluru from 2024-25. His research interests include the social life of built infrastructure and local-level democracy.

speakers.Name: Yogesh Nerpagar
speakers.Organization:
Center for youth development
and activities
speakers.Bio: Yogesh Nerpagar is the Assistant Director at the Centre for Youth Development and Activities, bringing over 10 years of experience in the development sector. He has led programs in youth empowerment, gender equality, skill development, and community engagement. Yogesh specializes in mentoring young professionals, facilitating career counselling, and implementing sustainable livelihood and social development initiatives. With a decade of hands-on experience, he is committed to driving meaningful impact and fostering inclusive growth across rural and urban communities.

speakers.Name: Zeel Patel
speakers.Bio:
Zeel Patel is a student of BCT (Bachelor’s in Construction Technology) at CEPT University, Ahmedabad, with academic and field-based experience in water-sensitive urban design, flood resilience, and Blue–Green Infrastructure (BGI) systems in Indian cities. His work focuses on evaluating nature-based solutions for urban flooding mitigation, groundwater recharge, and climate-resilient infrastructure, with particular emphasis on percolation wells and decentralized stormwater management systems.
He has conducted field documentation, hydrological analysis, and public perception studies related to urban waterlogging in Ahmedabad. His research integrates rainfall analysis, infiltration modelling and community feedback to assess the performance of BGI interventions in dense urban contexts. His academic interests include WASH, climate adaptation, sustainable urban drainage systems (SUDS) and nature-based solutions for cities in the Global South.

speakers.Name: Zenani Dludla
speakers.Organization: Bremen Overseas Research and Development Association (BORDA), South Africa
speakers.Bio:
Zenani Dludla is a Project Coordinator at BORDA SA. She has experience in both the environmental sector and the water and sanitation sector, and she is known for being organised, dedicated, and focused on delivering results.Zenani has worked on important projects that support healthier communities. She played a key role in the School Sanitation Programme, where she helped organise training for schools and taught infrastructure managers about good sanitation practices.
In her current role, she coordinates projects that aim to improve access to safe sanitation, supports the use of decentralised systems, and build skills within communities. Zenani holds a Bachelor of Social Science in Geography and Environmental Management and Honours degrees in Environmental Management. She is passionate about sustainability and community development.

general.name: Global South Academic Conclave 2026
general.description1: The Center for Water and Sanitation (CWAS) at CRDF, CEPT University is organising the third edition of Global South Academic Conclave (GSAC) on WASH and Climate in February 2026. The previous two editions in 2024 and 2025 were immensely successful, where more than 2000 participants from over 250 organisations across 35 countries joined us at these conclaves.
general.description2: To continue these discussions, we have organised this third edition of GSAC on 6th–7th February 2026 at CEPT University campus in Ahmedabad. It is being organised in collaboration with the Faculty of Planning, CEPT University, and it is supported by the Viega Foundation and Gates Foundation.
general.description3: The third edition of GSAC focuses on WASH Monitoring, Governance and Financing and WASH Innovations in the Global South. GSAC is visualised as a cross-learning event among sector partners, academia and researchers.
general.theme1_d: To showcase systems, policies and strategies for measuring and monitoring WASH outcomes in different countries.
general.theme2: Governance and Financing for inclusive and climate resilient WASH
general.theme2_d: To discuss the political, social, economic, financial and administrative systems that influence WASH services and its impacts on equity and climate resilience.
general.theme3: WASH innovations in technology and service delivery
general.theme3_d: To demonstrate innovations in WASH services management through technology, government programmes and community engagement.
